heading: Courageous Leadership For Florida Families.
text: Washington has been sold. It's time to take it back. Kelly is running for Congress to lower costs, defend health care, and bring opportunity home to the Gulf Coast.

heading: Washington Has Been Sold. Time To Take It Back.
text: We own this government — and it's time it worked that way again. For too long it's been run like a private club for lobbyists, the super wealthy, and corporations who can buy access, not the people who actually live here. So, we pay more for groceries, insurance, prescriptions, and rent while they pay less in taxes. Our kids inherit the debt while big donors pocket the tax breaks. Our neighbors rebuild after the storm on their own while the powerful rebuild their portfolios. What about us?

heading: Washington Has Been Sold. Time To Take It Back.
text: Here's the good news: this is fixable. Kelly Kirschner has spent his life fighting for people like us. When a developer tried to drop ten-story condos into single-family neighborhoods, he organized hundreds of residents, ran for office, and beat a well-funded incumbent with 75% of the vote. As Commissioner and Mayor, he took on and beat powerful interests like Florida Power & Light and predatory developers. To get big money out of local politics, he led the effort to pass the strongest local campaign finance reform in Florida — approved by more than 80% of voters. And just last year, as a private citizen, he helped stop a special-interest grab of the Ringling Museum.

heading: Washington Has Been Sold. Time To Take It Back.
text: He's ready to do it for us in Washington. Let's fix this.

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: A third-generation Floridian, Peace Corps volunteer, former Mayor of Sarasota, and a single father who built a non-profit lifting first-generation students into the country's top universities — debt-free.

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: Kelly Kirschner is a third-generation Floridian who grew up near the Sarasota-Bradenton airport, in the kind of neighborhood where a hard day's work was the baseline expectation. After school and on weekends, Kelly worked the family fruit stand, Blue Heron Fruit Shippers , selling oranges and grapefruit alongside the rest of his family. Those long hours and thin margins taught him early that most people aren't asking for much: an honest product, a fair price, and to be treated like they matter.

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: After earning his bachelor's and master's degrees from Georgetown University , on a full scholarship working as the head manager of the men's basketball team, Kelly chose a different path than his classmates. In 1999, he joined the Peace Corps , spending four years in northern Guatemala helping Mayan farming families reach new markets and grow household income. It was measurable, lasting work — not press releases.

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: Service is the Kirschner family's common thread; Kelly's brother served multiple tours as a U.S. Army officer in the Middle East and Afghanistan. That same conviction — that you owe something to a cause bigger than yourself — has anchored Kelly since he was a kid bagging tangerines at the Blue Heron.

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: Kelly has spent his life taking on the “untouchables” — and winning for those who have long been ignored.

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: Back home, Kelly proved he could deliver in the private sector, scaling sales at Manatee County's Bio-Pro Research from $60,000 to over $2.5 million in just three years . But the pull of public service remained. When Sarasota's government spent decades dodging its promise to fund Payne Park, Kelly organized his neighbors until the insiders ran out of excuses and the park was finally built. When a developer tried to drop ten-story condos into a single-family neighborhood, Kelly stopped them — and then ran for City Commission. He beat a well-funded incumbent who outspent him 3-to-1, winning with 75% of the vote .

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: As Commissioner and Mayor, Kelly took on the heavyweights. He led the passage of Florida's strongest local campaign finance reforms (approved by more than 80% of the electorate ), pushed FPL for unprecedented resident concessions, and clawed back millions for taxpayers by exposing a sweetheart lease at Marina Jacks. Most recently, in 2025, he stood with community leaders to stop special interests from seizing control of the Ringling Museum of Art.

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: Outside of City Hall, Kelly spent a decade raising his two children and building institutions that work. He grew UnidosNow into an organization that has helped over 1,000 first-generation students earn debt-free admission to elite universities, and led executive leadership development and lifelong learning programs as Vice President at Eckerd College .

heading: Florida Roots. Florida Fight.
text: The system has been rigged against ordinary families for too long. Kelly has spent his life taking on the “untouchables” — from the Guatemalan government, to predatory developers, to corporate monopolies — and winning for those who have long been ignored. He's running because protecting our kids and standing up for working families shouldn't be up for negotiation. It's time for a leader who knows that public service is a debt you owe your community, not a ladder for yourself.
